ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle ODC$ are similar figures with point O as the center of similarity and a similarity ratio of $1\colon2$. $\angle OCD=90^\circ$, and $CO=CD$. If $A(1, 0)$, what are the coordinates of point C?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $AC$, \\
since $CO=CD$ and $\angle OCD=90^\circ$, \\
therefore $\triangle OCD$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
thus $\angle COD=45^\circ$, \\
since $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle ODC$ are similar figures with center of similarity at $O$ and a similarity ratio of $1:2$, \\
thus $2OA=OD$, and $\triangle OAB$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
hence $A$ is the midpoint of $OD$, \\
therefore $AC \perp OD$ (the three lines of an isosceles triangle coincide), \\
thus $\triangle OAC$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
since $A(1,0)$, \\
thus $OA=AC=1$, \\
hence the coordinates of point $C$ are $\boxed{(1,1)}$.
